purpose: Reusable, sourced public professional-profile statements; evidence only, never recipient selection.
constraints: No professional-profile entry is an outreach target or finding of wrongdoing.
Profile statements and training dates do not establish involvement in a specific case, supervision, communications, conflict or culpability.
Article-specific identity matches, review routes and interpretive limitations are held in the article manifest; carry those limits whenever a case uses this evidence.
The original source statements include cautionary wording. Preserve it; do not treat a profile statement as proof of a reported event.
Use only when relevant to a competent investigator or legal reviewer; no community, spiritual, media or general-policy package may select these named facts by default.
Verify current licensure and material historical facts independently.

facts.fact: Stanford publicly lists a clinical associate professor in adult neurology, with general neurology practice.
The Stanford profile reports neurology residency completed at UCSF in 1996; that training does not establish involvement by UCSF in any alleged 2019 incident.
Official profile lists Chief of Neurology Clinics, 1999–2024.
Official profile lists Vice Chair for Clinical Services, 2015–2024, and neurology residency program director, 1999–2010.
UCSF public profile describes a neurologist specializing in movement disorders, including ataxia.
The UCSF profile lists a Stanford neurology residency completed in 2013 and a Stanford fellowship completed in 2014.
The UCSF Health clinical profile confirms Stanford residency and fellowship; title differs from the academic profile, so exact faculty rank should be checked directly if material.
